account:
Today has been outwardly routine: a mill grain inspection, office work, tea with my neighbour, and now the eighteen hundred great hall lighting inspection. Yet I have the feeling that people are coordinating something beyond ordinary business. The secretary, builder, and innkeeper have repeatedly emphasised a seventeen thirty gathering and accompanying me into the hall. I did not recall that gathering, though the secretary says I agreed this morning. The written addendum does confirm that I approved the lighting inspection yesterday, covering eight lanterns and four tables, so the inspection itself is not unexplained. The innkeeper says he arranged the gathering with the builder, and everyone insists there is no separate agenda.

My neighbour knew the lighting was ready, had spoken with the builder and several neighbours near the bakery, and encouraged putting town business aside during tea. Now the builder asks what town improvement has made me proudest. The baker is also waiting near the town hall entrance, though I have not heard why. Together these details suggest a possible friendly or celebratory gathering under cover of the inspection, perhaps something meant for me, but that is only a suspicion. I have seen no direct evidence of preparations beyond what people have said.

There are also vague rumours of bridge or port changes, repeated by Townsfolk Eighteen, but the secretary reports no council letters or firsthand confirmation from freight or the builder. My neighbour likewise knew nothing definite. I should not treat those rumours as actual changes or assume they are connected to the gathering. For now, I am with the innkeeper, builder, and secretary just before eighteen hundred, ready to attend the scheduled inspection and learn what is actually happening.
